response.message:
I've drawn a first IBM Cloud sketch on the board. A pull-request event triggers a reviewer job on IBM Code Engine. The job gets a short-lived, read-only token from IBM Secrets Manager, fetches only the authorised diff and related files, and checks scope through a guard before calling a watsonx.ai model. It then drafts review comments tied to the changed lines, logs each run to IBM Cloud Logs, and sends the drafts to a person to approve. It never pushes, merges or runs repository code.

**First local test:** we run the reviewer against a synthetic pull request from a fixture repository, with the model replaced by scripted responses. That proves the plumbing works: the scope filtering, the line anchoring, and the rule that nothing is ever written to the repository. It does not prove review quality. Checking quality needs real watsonx.ai calls against an agreed set of known defects, and that also depends on model access, region and account approval. None of those have been checked yet, and nothing has been deployed.

I've recorded IBM Cloud as the chosen platform, but no region is picked yet. Which Git host holds the repository: GitHub, GitLab or something else? And should the approved comments be posted back as a pending pull-request review (which needs comment-write permission), or stay in a report?

proposal.title: IBM Cloud AI pull-request reviewer (read-only, draft comments)
proposal.body: End-to-end sketch: existing repository → Code Engine reviewer job (read-only token from Secrets Manager) → scope guard → watsonx.ai → draft line-linked comments for human approval, with audit logs. Assumptions: Git host, region, model ID and comment write-back are undecided; no deployment, region or account access is verified. Repository code is never executed, pushed or merged.

response.message: The emulation shows the design itself is sound: there are no failures, and the board still keeps the full end-to-end flow. Every blocker is there because the tool has no native generator for this IBM Cloud pull-request reviewer (Code Engine, Secrets Manager, watsonx.ai, IBM Cloud Logs). Changing the graph can't fix that, and the narrow storage-only setup would cut the scope, so we won't use it. Closing that gap is product engineering work: someone needs to build the generator and runtime code, with this artifact (ae8a69f8…, revision 2) as the reproducer. The first gap is the repo → reviewer connection. Which Git host and trigger should that connection use: GitHub with a webhook, GitLab, or something else? That choice sets the read-only token scope and the first acceptance test.
